tasks.prompt: Order the conductivity measurement steps for a drinking water sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory measuring conductivity as a general chemistry parameter.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing the conductivity cell through recording the result.

cards.label: Verify the conductivity cell with the specified potassium chloride standard
Rinse the cell three times with the sample to be measured
Immerse the cell in the sample ensuring no air bubbles cling to the electrodes
Allow the temperature compensated reading to stabilize
Record the conductivity and the sample temperature
Rinse the cell with purified water and store it as the manufacturer directs

tasks.explanation: The cell is verified against a standard and rinsed with sample before immersion, and a bubble free, stabilized, temperature compensated reading is what gets recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order the ultraviolet absorbance at 254 nm measurement steps.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory measuring UV 254 as an organics indicator on treated water.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing the spectrophotometer through recording the absorbance.

cards.label: Warm up the spectrophotometer and set the wavelength to 254 nm
Filter the sample through the specified filter to remove turbidity interference
Rinse the quartz cell with filtered sample and fill it without bubbles
Blank the instrument with purified water in a matched quartz cell
Read the sample absorbance and record it with the cell path length
Clean and store the quartz cells protected from scratching

tasks.explanation: UV 254 uses quartz cells and a filtered sample because ordinary glass absorbs ultraviolet light and turbidity scatters it, and the blank sets the zero before the sample is read.

tasks.prompt: Order the sample digestion steps before metals analysis.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory preparing drinking water samples for metals analysis by acid digestion.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the logged samples through digested samples ready for the instrument.

cards.label: Verify the sample preservation and acidification meet the method requirements
Measure the specified sample volume into the digestion vessel
Add the specified acids in the fume hood wearing the required protective equipment
Heat the digestion by the method program until the digestion is complete
Cool the vessels and bring each digest to the specified final volume
Label the digests and transfer them to the instrument analyst with the batch record

tasks.explanation: Digestion converts the sample into a clear acid solution of defined volume, done in order in the fume hood, so the instrument measures the total metal content of the original sample.

tasks.prompt: Order the instrument batch setup steps for metals analysis.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory setting up an inductively coupled plasma batch for drinking water metals.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing calibration standards through starting the sample run.

cards.label: Prepare the calibration standards and the initial calibration verification standard
Warm up and tune the instrument and confirm the tune criteria pass
Run the calibration standards and confirm the calibration meets the method criteria
Analyze the calibration verification and blank and confirm both are acceptable
Load the samples with quality control samples placed through the sequence
Start the run and record the batch identity in the instrument log

tasks.explanation: The batch is built so calibration is proven by an independent verification standard and blank before any sample runs, with quality controls spaced through the sequence.

tasks.prompt: Order the jar test steps an analyst runs to support coagulant dose selection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory jar testing the current raw water for the treatment plant.
tasks.configuration: Scope: collecting the raw water through recommending a dose to operations.

cards.label: Collect a fresh raw water sample and measure turbidity, pH, alkalinity, and temperature
Fill each jar with the same measured volume of raw water
Add a different coagulant dose to each jar at the start of rapid mixing
Rapid mix briefly, then slow mix to simulate flocculation
Stop mixing and allow the specified settling period
Measure settled water turbidity in each jar and report the best performing dose

tasks.explanation: The jar test mirrors the plant sequence at bench scale, and the dose recommendation comes from settled turbidity compared across identical jars that differ only in dose.

tasks.prompt: Order the chlorine demand test steps for a raw water sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory determining the chlorine demand of a source water.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing the dosed sample series through calculating the demand.

cards.label: Prepare a series of sample portions and dose each with a different known chlorine dose
Mix each portion and store them in the dark for the specified contact time
Measure the free chlorine residual remaining in each portion after contact
Select the portion whose residual matches the target residual for the plant
Calculate demand as the dose applied minus the residual measured for that portion
Report the demand and the dose needed to meet the target residual

tasks.explanation: Demand is found by dosing a series, holding for the contact time, and measuring what chlorine remains, because demand is the difference between what was added and what survived.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to prepare a working calibration standard from a stock standard.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory preparing a working standard by serial dilution.
tasks.configuration: Scope: selecting the stock standard through labelling the working standard.

cards.label: Confirm the stock standard identity, concentration, and expiry date
Calculate the volumes needed to reach the target working concentration
Pipette the calculated stock volume into a clean volumetric flask
Dilute to the mark with the specified diluent and mix thoroughly
Transfer the working standard to a clean labelled container
Record the preparation with stock lot, volumes, date, and analyst in the standards log

tasks.explanation: A working standard is only as good as its traceability: stock identity and expiry are confirmed first, volumes are calculated before pipetting, and the preparation is logged in full.

tasks.prompt: Order the DPD reagent verification steps when a new reagent lot is opened.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory opening a new lot of DPD reagent for chlorine analysis.
tasks.configuration: Scope: opening the new lot through releasing it for routine use.

cards.label: Record the new lot number, receipt date, and expiry in the reagent inventory
Inspect the reagent for moisture damage, discolouration, or broken seals
Analyze a known chlorine standard with the new lot reagent
Analyze the same standard with the current lot reagent for comparison
Confirm the two lots agree within the acceptance limit
Release the new lot for use and file the verification record

tasks.explanation: A new reagent lot is released by agreement with the proven lot on a known standard, so a defective lot is caught before it touches a compliance result.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily analytical balance verification steps.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory performing its morning balance check before weighing standards.
tasks.configuration: Scope: approaching the balance through releasing it for the day work.

cards.label: Inspect the balance pan and chamber and confirm the balance is level and clean
Allow the balance to warm up and complete its internal adjustment
Place the calibrated check weights on the pan one at a time and record each reading
Compare each reading with the acceptance limits for that weight
Record the verification and analyst initials on the daily check sheet
Remove the balance from service and report it if any weight fails the limits

tasks.explanation: Balance verification uses calibrated weights across the working range before any standard is weighed, and a failure takes the balance out of service rather than letting suspect weighings proceed.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to assemble a quality control batch for a chemistry analysis.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory building a batch of twenty samples with full quality controls.
tasks.configuration: Scope: listing the samples through releasing the assembled batch to the analyst.

cards.label: List the samples in the batch and confirm each is within its holding time
Insert a method blank at the start of the batch sequence
Insert a laboratory control sample of known concentration in the batch
Select samples for a duplicate and a matrix spike at the method frequency
Arrange the sequence so quality controls bracket the field samples
Record the batch composition on the bench worksheet and release it for analysis

tasks.explanation: A quality batch is designed before analysis: blanks, known controls, duplicates, and spikes are placed deliberately through the sequence so the batch can prove its own accuracy and precision.

tasks.prompt: Order the calibration curve review steps before samples are quantified.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory reviewing a multi point calibration for a chemistry method.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the instrument finishing the standards through accepting the calibration.

cards.label: Confirm every calibration standard was analyzed in the correct sequence
Check the calibration fit and the correlation criteria against the method limits
Examine each standard back calculated concentration for bias
Run and evaluate the independent calibration verification standard
Confirm the calibration blank shows no significant response
Accept the calibration and authorize sample quantification in the run record

tasks.explanation: A curve is accepted on evidence: fit, back calculated bias, an independent verification standard, and a clean blank together prove the calibration before any sample value is trusted.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to update a quality control chart after a batch is accepted.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory maintaining control charts for its laboratory control samples.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the accepted batch control result through filing the updated chart.

cards.label: Calculate the laboratory control sample recovery for the accepted batch
Plot the recovery on the control chart for that method and analyte
Compare the point with the warning and control limits on the chart
Check for trends such as consecutive points rising or falling
Initial and date the chart entry and note any trend or limit action taken
File the updated chart and report any control limit exceedance for follow up

tasks.explanation: Charting turns a single recovery into a trend record: the point is plotted, judged against limits and recent history, and exceedances are escalated rather than merely recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order the first steps when a method blank shows contamination.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional chemistry batch where the method blank returned a detectable result.
tasks.configuration: Scope: noticing the blank result through deciding the batch disposition path.

cards.label: Confirm the blank result and check the calculation and instrument entry for error
Quarantine the batch results so nothing is reported while the blank is investigated
Inspect reagent water, reagents, and glassware used for the batch
Prepare and analyze a fresh blank with new reagents and cleaned glassware
Compare the fresh blank result with the original blank result
Decide with the senior analyst whether the batch can be qualified or must be rerun

tasks.explanation: The batch is quarantined before investigation so no result escapes, the likely contamination sources are checked with a fresh blank, and qualification or rerun is a documented senior decision.

tasks.prompt: Order the duplicate precision review steps for a completed batch.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory reviewing duplicate results for a chemistry batch.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the duplicate pair results through the precision disposition.

cards.label: Identify the duplicate pair and confirm both were prepared from the same sample
Calculate the relative percent difference between the two results
Compare the relative percent difference with the method acceptance limit
Review the sample matrix notes for reasons the sample may be non homogeneous
Accept the precision or flag the batch for investigation if the limit is exceeded
Record the calculation and disposition on the batch quality sheet

tasks.explanation: Precision review starts by confirming the pair truly came from one sample, then judges the relative percent difference against the limit, with matrix notes considered before a batch is flagged.

tasks.prompt: Order the matrix spike recovery review steps for a completed batch.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory reviewing a spiked sample in a chemistry batch.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the spiked and unspiked results through the accuracy disposition.

cards.label: Confirm the spike amount added and the unspiked sample result
Calculate the spike recovery from the spiked result minus the native result
Compare the recovery with the method acceptance range
Review dilution and matrix notes that could explain a biased recovery
Accept the accuracy or flag the affected results for qualification
Record the recovery calculation and disposition on the batch quality sheet

tasks.explanation: Spike recovery isolates accuracy in the real matrix: the native result is subtracted, recovery is judged against the range, and biased recoveries lead to qualification, not silent reporting.

tasks.prompt: Order the proficiency testing sample workflow from receipt to submission.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory participating in an external proficiency testing round.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the proficiency samples arriving through submitting the results to the provider.

cards.label: Log the proficiency samples on receipt and store them exactly as instructed
Assign the samples to an analyst who runs the method routinely
Analyze the samples by the routine method with no special treatment
Review the results through the normal data review path only
Submit the results to the provider by the round deadline
File the provider evaluation when it arrives and record any required follow up

tasks.explanation: Proficiency samples prove routine competence, so they are handled and analyzed exactly like client samples, reviewed normally, and submitted on time.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to schedule quality control samples across a week of batches.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory planning quality control placement for a busy analysis week.
tasks.configuration: Scope: reviewing the week sample load through issuing the quality control plan.

cards.label: Review the expected batches and sample counts for each method for the week
Apply the method quality control frequencies to calculate the controls needed
Confirm control materials, spikes, and standards are in stock for the plan
Schedule the controls into each batch sequence on the planning board
Brief the analysts on the quality control plan at the week start meeting
Record the issued plan in the quality records

tasks.explanation: Quality control is planned from batch volume and method frequency, stock is confirmed before the week begins, and analysts are briefed so controls are never skipped under time pressure.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps when an instrument calibration due date arrives.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory bench meter reaching its scheduled calibration date.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the due date notice through returning the meter to service.

cards.label: Remove the meter from routine use and tag it as due for calibration
Clean and inspect the meter, probes, and cables before calibration
Calibrate the meter with traceable standards across its working range
Verify the calibration with an independent standard not used in calibration
Record the calibration, standards used, and results in the equipment file
Return the meter to service with a new calibration due label

tasks.explanation: A due meter leaves service first, is calibrated with traceable standards, and is verified independently before its new due label returns it to routine work.

tasks.prompt: Order the receipt steps for a new certified reference standard.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory receiving a certified reference material for metals analysis.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the standard arriving through its entry in the standards inventory.

cards.label: Check the shipment against the order and inspect the container for damage
Verify the certificate values, lot number, and expiry date on the certificate
Record the standard in the inventory with its certified value and uncertainty
Store the standard at the temperature and conditions on its certificate
Assign the standard its laboratory identification code
Brief analysts that the new lot is in service and retire the old lot record

tasks.explanation: A certified standard is accepted on its certificate, stored exactly as certified, and given a traceable identity before analysts rely on its value.

tasks.prompt: Order the monthly quality control trend review steps.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory holding its monthly quality review.
tasks.configuration: Scope: gathering the month charts through assigning the review actions.

cards.label: Gather the control charts, proficiency results, and nonconformance records for the month
Review each chart for limit exceedances, trends, and shifts
Review open nonconformances and check that corrective actions are on schedule
Agree any method, training, or equipment actions arising from the review
Assign each action an owner and a completion date
Record and file the review minutes in the quality records

tasks.explanation: The monthly review connects charts, proficiency, and nonconformances into owned, dated actions, so quality signals become improvements instead of filed paperwork.

tasks.prompt: Order the second source verification steps for a calibration.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory verifying a calibration with a standard from a different supplier lot.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing the second source standard through accepting the calibration.

cards.label: Prepare the second source standard at a mid range concentration from the independent lot
Analyze the second source standard immediately after calibration
Compare the measured value with its certified or prepared value
Confirm the agreement is within the method acceptance limit
Record the verification with both lot numbers in the run record
Proceed to samples only after the verification passes

tasks.explanation: A second source standard is independent of the calibration standards, so its agreement proves the calibration is accurate rather than merely repeatable.

tasks.prompt: Order the continuing calibration verification steps during a long instrument run.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory running a long metals sequence with periodic checks.
tasks.configuration: Scope: reaching the check interval through deciding whether the run continues.

cards.label: Analyze the continuing calibration verification standard at the method interval
Compare the measured value with the true value and calculate the percent difference
Confirm the difference is within the method acceptance limit
Continue the run if the check passes and record the result in the sequence
Stop the run and recalibrate if the check fails
Reanalyze the samples since the last passing check after recalibration

tasks.explanation: Continuing checks bracket the run: samples are only as valid as the last passing check, so a failure stops the run and the samples since that check are rerun after recalibration.

tasks.prompt: Order the laboratory control sample preparation steps.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory preparing a control sample from a certified material.
tasks.configuration: Scope: selecting the certified material through storing the prepared control.

cards.label: Select the certified material matching the method matrix and analyte range
Calculate the preparation needed to reach the target control concentration
Prepare the control exactly by the documented procedure
Verify the prepared control by analyzing it against a current calibration
Confirm the measured value agrees with the target within the preparation limits
Label and store the control with its target value, date, and expiry

tasks.explanation: A control sample is prepared to a known target and proven by measurement before use, because a control of uncertain value cannot judge a batch.

tasks.prompt: Order the first response steps when a batch quality control sample fails.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional chemistry batch where the laboratory control sample recovery is outside limits.
tasks.configuration: Scope: seeing the failed recovery through placing the batch on hold.

cards.label: Confirm the failure by rechecking the calculation and the raw instrument data
Place the entire batch on hold so no results can be reported
Notify the senior analyst or quality designate of the failure
Record the failure in the nonconformance log with the batch identity
Preserve the samples, extracts, and raw data for investigation
Begin the documented investigation before any rerun is authorized

tasks.explanation: A failed control stops reporting first: the failure is verified, the batch is held, supervision is notified, and evidence is preserved before investigation begins.

tasks.prompt: Order the rerun decision steps after a quality control investigation.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory deciding the disposition of a held chemistry batch.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the investigation findings through the documented disposition.

cards.label: Review the investigation findings and identify whether a cause was found
Confirm whether the original samples remain within holding time and volume
Decide whether a full rerun, a partial rerun, or qualification is appropriate
Obtain senior analyst approval for the chosen disposition
Carry out the rerun or apply the qualification to the held results
Close the nonconformance with the disposition and its justification recorded

tasks.explanation: The disposition follows the evidence: holding time and volume decide if a rerun is even possible, senior approval is required, and the justification is recorded when the case closes.

tasks.prompt: Order the response when a calibration verification standard fails.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory where the verification standard reads outside its acceptance limit.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the failed verification through returning the instrument to service.

cards.label: Stop the analysis sequence and hold any samples already run
Prepare a fresh verification standard and analyze it once
Inspect the calibration standards and instrument for an obvious cause if it fails again
Recalibrate the instrument with fresh standards
Verify the new calibration with the independent verification standard
Reanalyze any held samples under the verified calibration before reporting

tasks.explanation: One fresh standard distinguishes a preparation error from a calibration problem, and if recalibration is needed, held samples are rerun under the proven calibration.

tasks.prompt: Order the contamination source investigation steps for a contaminated blank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory tracing contamination found in a method blank.
tasks.configuration: Scope: assigning the investigation through confirming the source found.

cards.label: Analyze a blank of reagent water alone to test the water supply
Analyze a blank carried through clean glassware only to test the glassware
Analyze a blank with fresh reagent lots to test the reagents
Compare the three results to isolate which component carries the contamination
Correct the isolated source by replacement, cleaning, or repair
Analyze a full method blank to confirm the contamination is cleared before batches resume

tasks.explanation: The investigation changes one component at a time, water, glassware, then reagents, so the comparison isolates the source, and a clean full blank proves the fix.

tasks.prompt: Order the investigation when duplicate precision fails repeatedly.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory seeing repeated duplicate failures on one method.
tasks.configuration: Scope: recognizing the pattern through implementing the corrective action.

cards.label: Review the recent duplicate results and confirm the failures share a method or matrix
Check sample homogenization and subsampling steps in the procedure
Observe the analyst technique for the preparation step in question
Analyze a homogeneous control sample in duplicate to test the method itself
Identify whether the cause is sample handling, technique, or the samples themselves
Revise the procedure or retrain as the cause requires and document the action

tasks.explanation: Repeated failures are investigated as a pattern: the method is tested on a homogeneous control to separate technique and handling causes from genuine sample variability.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to evaluate a matrix spike failure on a difficult sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory with a low spike recovery on a high colour sample.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the failed recovery through the reported qualified result.

cards.label: Confirm the spike calculation and the spike amount added
Analyze the sample at a dilution and respike the diluted portion
Compare the diluted spike recovery with the original recovery
Conclude whether matrix interference explains the original failure
Report the sample result with the matrix qualification and its explanation
Record the investigation in the batch nonconformance notes

tasks.explanation: Dilution reduces matrix interference, so a recovering diluted spike confirms the matrix as the cause and supports a qualified, explained result instead of a silent one.

tasks.prompt: Order the response when an instrument shows drift across a run.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory noticing steadily rising check standard values during a run.
tasks.configuration: Scope: noticing the drift trend through restoring a stable run.

cards.label: Confirm the drift by analyzing the check standard again
Stop the run at the last check that was within limits
Inspect the instrument for the drift cause such as a failing lamp or dirty cell
Correct the cause and recalibrate the instrument
Verify stability with repeated check standards over a short series
Restart the run and reanalyze samples back to the last acceptable check

tasks.explanation: Drift invalidates results gradually, so the run is cut back to the last good check, the cause is fixed, stability is proven, and affected samples are rerun.

tasks.prompt: Order the response when an analyst discovers an expired standard was used.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory finding that a calibration used a standard past its expiry.
tasks.configuration: Scope: discovering the expiry through the final disposition of affected results.

cards.label: Identify every batch and result produced with the expired standard
Place all affected results on hold and notify the senior analyst
Assess the standard condition and any stability information available
Recalibrate with an in date standard and reanalyze retained samples where possible
Qualify or withdraw results that cannot be reanalyzed
Complete a nonconformance record with the extent and corrective actions

tasks.explanation: The response starts with the full extent of use, holds everything affected, and rebuilds results with valid standards, withdrawing what cannot be rebuilt.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to notify a client that reported results are being revised.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory that must amend a report after a quality failure is confirmed.
tasks.configuration: Scope: confirming the failure affects issued results through issuing the amended report.

cards.label: Confirm which issued reports contain results affected by the failure
Notify the client contact that an amended report will be issued and why
Correct or reanalyze the affected results under valid quality control
Prepare the amended report clearly marked as amended with the changes identified
Issue the amended report and confirm the client received it
File the original report, the amendment, and the notification record together

tasks.explanation: Amending a report requires prompt honest notification, a clearly marked amended report, and a filed trail linking the original, the correction, and the client notice.

tasks.prompt: Order the preventive action steps after a recurring quality control failure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory addressing the third similar failure in a quarter.
tasks.configuration: Scope: recognizing the recurrence through verifying the preventive action worked.

cards.label: Review the related nonconformance records and define the recurring pattern
Determine the root cause using the investigation evidence across the cases
Select a preventive action that removes the root cause, not only the symptom
Implement the action with an owner and a completion date
Monitor the following batches for the defined effectiveness period
Close the action only after the monitoring shows the failure has not recurred

tasks.explanation: Preventive action is judged by results: the pattern and root cause are defined across cases, the fix is owned and dated, and closure waits for monitored proof.

tasks.prompt: Order the second person data review steps for a completed batch.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory applying independent review before results are reported.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the analyst submitting the batch through the reviewer releasing it.

cards.label: Analyst completes calculations and assembles raw data, charts, and quality results
Reviewer checks sample identities and transcription from raw data to results
Reviewer recalculates a selection of results independently
Reviewer confirms all quality controls met the acceptance criteria
Reviewer returns any errors to the analyst for correction and recheck
Reviewer signs the release and routes the batch to reporting

tasks.explanation: Independent review checks identity, transcription, calculation, and quality acceptance in that order, and only a signed release moves results to reporting.

tasks.prompt: Order the result finalization steps from instrument value to reported value.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory finalizing chemistry results for a client report.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the raw calculated result through the value entered on the report.

cards.label: Confirm the raw result and its units from the calculation record
Apply any dilution factor from the preparation record
Compare the result with the method reporting limit
Apply the method rounding and significant figure rules
Enter the final value and qualifier, if any, into the reporting system
Verify the entered value against the calculation record before the report is issued

tasks.explanation: Finalization applies dilution, reporting limit, and rounding rules in order, and the entered value is verified against the calculation before it can appear on a report.

tasks.prompt: Order the report assembly steps for a drinking water sample set.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory preparing a certificate of analysis for a municipal client.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the released results through the signed report ready to send.

cards.label: Gather the released results for every sample and parameter in the set
Check the report header for the correct client, system, and sampling dates
Confirm each result carries its units, method reference, and any qualifiers
Confirm the report notes any holding time or quality qualifications
Have the report reviewed and signed by the authorized signatory
Issue the report to the client and file the issued copy

tasks.explanation: A report is assembled from released results only, checked for identity, units, and qualifications, and signed by an authorized signatory before it is issued and filed.

tasks.prompt: Order the laboratory reporting steps when a result exceeds an Ontario standard.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory with an E. coli positive drinking water result under Regulation 169/03.
tasks.configuration: Scope: confirming the result through completing the laboratory notifications.

cards.label: Confirm the result through the method confirmation steps
Notify the client system contact by telephone immediately and note the time and person
Notify the local health unit and the ministry as the regulation requires for laboratories
Follow the telephone notices with the written adverse result notice
Record every notification with date, time, and recipient in the adverse file
Provide the client with the resampling requirements and laboratory availability

tasks.explanation: An adverse laboratory result triggers immediate telephone notification before paperwork, with health unit and ministry notice, written follow up, and a complete notification record.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to report a result below the method detection limit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory reporting a chemistry parameter not detected in a sample.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the instrument showing no significant response through the reported value.

cards.label: Confirm the instrument response is below the method detection limit criteria
Confirm the batch blank and quality controls support a not detected conclusion
Check the reporting limit that applies to this client and method
Enter the result as not detected with the reporting limit value as specified
Add the method reference so the client can interpret the result
Verify the entry in the report review step

tasks.explanation: A not detected report rests on the batch evidence, especially the blank and controls, and is reported with its limit and method so the client knows what the result means.

tasks.prompt: Order the data entry verification steps for hand entered bench results.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory entering titration results from paper bench sheets.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the completed bench sheets through the verified system records.

cards.label: Enter each result into the system directly from the bench sheet
Print or display the entered results beside the bench sheet values
Compare every entered value, unit, and qualifier with the bench sheet
Correct any transcription error and note the correction
Have a second person verify the entries for compliance samples
File the bench sheets with the batch record after verification

tasks.explanation: Hand entry is verified value by value against the bench sheet, with a second person check for compliance data, because transcription is a common and preventable error source.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to prepare a monthly sampling summary for a municipal client.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory summarizing a month of results for a drinking water system.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pulling the month results through issuing the summary.

cards.label: Extract all results reported for the system during the month
Check the extracted list against the sampling schedule for completeness
Summarize the results by parameter with any exceedances highlighted
Confirm every exceedance in the summary matches its adverse record
Review and approve the summary through the normal signatory path
Issue the summary to the client and file it with the month records

tasks.explanation: The monthly summary is reconciled against the sampling schedule so missing samples are as visible as exceedances, and every highlighted exceedance is tied to its adverse record.

tasks.prompt: Order the verification steps before a new calculation spreadsheet is used for reporting.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory introducing a spreadsheet for alkalinity calculations.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the drafted spreadsheet through its approval for routine use.

cards.label: Enter test data with hand calculated expected results into the spreadsheet
Compare every spreadsheet output with the hand calculated values
Test the spreadsheet with edge cases such as zero and maximum titration volumes
Lock the formula cells and record the spreadsheet version
Have the spreadsheet checked and approved by a second analyst
Release the approved version and withdraw any draft copies

tasks.explanation: A reporting spreadsheet is proven against hand calculations including edge cases, then locked and version controlled so analysts use only the verified tool.

tasks.prompt: Order the record filing steps at the completion of a sample set.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory closing out a completed drinking water sample file.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the issued report through the file entering archive storage.

cards.label: Collect the custody form, bench sheets, raw data, and quality records for the set
Check the file against the record checklist for completeness
Resolve any missing record before the file is closed
Scan or file the records in the sample number order used by the archive
Record the archive location and retention date in the index
Move the closed file to the archive storage area

tasks.explanation: A complete file is checked against the checklist before archiving, because records that cannot be retrieved cannot defend a result years later.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to answer a client query about a reported result.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory responding to a client question about a low chlorine result.
tasks.configuration: Scope: receiving the query through closing the response record.

cards.label: Log the query with the client, sample identity, and the result in question
Retrieve the full batch record including raw data and quality controls
Review the result, field chlorine record, and any qualifiers applied
Prepare an explanation that answers the query from the record evidence
Respond to the client and offer resampling if the query remains unresolved
File the query, the evidence reviewed, and the response in the sample file

tasks.explanation: A result query is answered from the retrieved record, not from memory, and the whole exchange is filed so the explanation remains traceable to its evidence.

tasks.prompt: Order the analyst support steps during an adverse water quality incident.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario system responding to an adverse bacteriological result under Regulation 170/03.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the analyst learning of the incident through the resample results being reported.

cards.label: Confirm the adverse result details and the locations requiring resampling
Prepare the sterile bottles and custody forms for the resampling run
Brief the sampler on locations, residuals to record, and priority delivery
Receive the resamples as priority and start analysis without queue delay
Report the resample results to the system contact as soon as they are confirmed
File all incident records, results, and notifications in the adverse file

tasks.explanation: The analyst supports the incident end to end: resampling materials ready, priority analysis, immediate reporting of resample results, and a complete incident file.

tasks.prompt: Order the laboratory support steps after a boil water advisory is issued.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional community under a boil water advisory following an adverse result.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the advisory being issued through the laboratory role in lifting it.

cards.label: Record the advisory details and the clearance criteria set by the health unit
Schedule the clearance sampling locations and frequency with the system operator
Analyze clearance samples as priority on each sampling day
Report each clearance result to the operator and health unit contact promptly
Confirm when the required consecutive satisfactory results are complete
File the clearance record set with the original adverse file

tasks.explanation: Laboratory support for an advisory is driven by the health unit clearance criteria, with priority analysis and prompt reporting until the required satisfactory results are complete.

tasks.prompt: Order the support steps when a chemical parameter exceeds the Ontario standard.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory confirming a result above a Regulation 169/03 chemical standard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the first result above standard through the confirmation sampling outcome.

cards.label: Verify the original result through data review and quality control records
Analyze a retained portion or duplicate to confirm the result if the method allows
Notify the client system contact with the confirmed exceedance details
Arrange confirmation sampling at the location as the client directs
Analyze the confirmation sample as priority and report it promptly
File the exceedance, confirmation, and notification records together

tasks.explanation: A chemical exceedance is verified and confirmed before notification where the method allows, then followed by priority confirmation sampling so decisions rest on solid data.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to activate the weekend adverse notification roster.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory receiving an adverse result on a Saturday afternoon.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the adverse result being confirmed Saturday through notifications completed.

cards.label: Confirm the adverse result and identify the notifications required
Contact the on call analyst or designate from the weekend roster
Make the client and health unit telephone notifications from the roster contacts
Record each notification time, recipient, and information given
Send the written adverse notice by the method in the procedure
Brief the Monday staff in writing on the incident status

tasks.explanation: The weekend roster turns an out of hours adverse result into the same disciplined notifications, with a written Monday handover so the incident never depends on one person memory.

tasks.prompt: Order the stand down steps when resamples clear an adverse incident.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario system whose resamples have all returned satisfactory.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the final satisfactory resample result through closing the incident file.

cards.label: Confirm all required resample sets are complete and satisfactory
Notify the system contact and the health unit of the complete results
Confirm with the health unit whether any advisory can be lifted
Provide the client with the full result set for their records
Complete the incident summary with actions, results, and notifications
Close and file the adverse incident record

tasks.explanation: Stand down requires the complete satisfactory resample set, notification to the health unit, and a finished incident summary, so closure is documented rather than assumed.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to assemble the adverse incident record package.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory compiling the file for an adverse incident review.
tasks.configuration: Scope: gathering the incident documents through the indexed package.

cards.label: Collect the original result record and its quality control evidence
Collect the notification records with dates, times, and recipients
Collect the resampling custody forms and result records
Collect the client and health unit correspondence for the incident
Index the package in chronological order with a cover summary
File the package and record its location for future reference

tasks.explanation: The package is built chronologically from result, notifications, resampling, and correspondence, with a cover summary, so a reviewer can reconstruct the whole incident.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to update adverse notification contact lists.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory reviewing its notification contacts at the start of the year.
tasks.configuration: Scope: starting the review through issuing the updated lists.

cards.label: Collect the current contact lists for clients, health units, and ministry contacts
Verify each telephone number and contact name with the organization
Record personnel changes, new numbers, and after hours contacts
Update the master notification list and the laboratory copy
Distribute the updated lists to every location where notifications are made
File the verification record and withdraw the superseded lists

tasks.explanation: Notification lists are verified directly with each organization and old copies are withdrawn, because an adverse call to a wrong number is a failed notification.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps to run an adverse notification practice drill.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory testing its adverse response with a simulated result.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planning the drill through filing the drill evaluation.

cards.label: Prepare a simulated adverse result clearly marked as a drill scenario
Deliver the scenario to the analyst on duty without prior notice of the timing
Observe the analyst completing the notification steps using the drill contacts
Record the time taken and any steps missed or delayed
Review the performance with the analyst and identify improvements
File the drill evaluation and assign any corrective actions

tasks.explanation: A drill tests the real response path with a marked scenario and drill contacts, and its value is the timed evaluation and the improvements it assigns.

tasks.prompt: Order the laboratory chemical spill response steps for a small acid spill.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory with a small hydrochloric acid spill on a bench.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the spill occurring through the area returning to use.

cards.label: Alert nearby staff and keep people away from the spill area
Put on the required protective equipment from the spill kit
Contain the spill with absorbent pads working from the outside inward
Neutralize and collect the contained residue as the spill procedure directs
Place the collected waste in the labelled chemical waste container
Report the spill, complete the incident record, and restock the spill kit

tasks.explanation: Spill response protects people first, contains from the outside inward so the spill does not spread, and ends with reporting and a restocked kit.

tasks.prompt: Order the monthly fume hood performance check steps.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory checking the hood used for acid digestion.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing for the check through recording the result.

cards.label: Clear the hood work area and set the sash at the marked operating height
Allow the hood ventilation to run until airflow is stable
Measure the face velocity at the specified points across the sash opening
Compare the average velocity with the laboratory acceptance range
Record the measurements and the hood status on the check form
Remove the hood from service and report it if the velocity fails the range

tasks.explanation: The hood is checked at its real working sash height with the area set as used, and a failed velocity takes it out of service because containment cannot be assumed.

tasks.prompt: Order the chemical waste accumulation steps at the laboratory bench.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory filling a waste container with spent acid solutions.
tasks.configuration: Scope: starting a new waste container through transferring a full one to storage.

cards.label: Select the correct waste container and confirm it is compatible with the waste
Label the container with the waste identity and the accumulation start date
Add waste through a funnel, keeping the container closed between additions
Stop filling at the marked maximum fill level
Close the full container and move it to the designated waste storage area
Record the container in the waste log and arrange pickup before its deadline

tasks.explanation: Waste containers are labelled from the first addition, kept closed, and never overfilled, with the log ensuring pickup happens inside the accumulation deadline.

tasks.prompt: Order the end of day laboratory housekeeping steps.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory closing after a normal analysis day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the last analyses finishing through the laboratory secured for the night.

cards.label: Return samples to their refrigerated storage locations and confirm temperatures
Wipe down benches and place glassware in the washing area
Check that gas, water, and equipment left running are set as required overnight
Empty bench waste into the correct waste streams
Record any issue for the morning staff in the handover note
Turn off lights, lock the laboratory, and set the alarm as required

tasks.explanation: Closing restores the laboratory to a known state: samples stored, benches clear, overnight equipment verified, and any issue handed over in writing.

tasks.prompt: Order the monthly personal protective equipment inspection steps.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory inspecting its shared protective equipment.
tasks.configuration: Scope: gathering the equipment through returning it to service.

cards.label: Gather gloves, eye protection, aprons, and respirator equipment for inspection
Inspect each item for damage, contamination, or expiry
Remove and tag any item that fails the inspection
Replace the failed items from stock and record the replacements
Clean and return the serviceable equipment to its storage locations
File the inspection record with the items checked and actions taken

tasks.explanation: Inspection removes failed equipment from service immediately and replaces it, so the record shows protection was verified, not assumed.

tasks.prompt: Order the training sequence for a newly hired laboratory analyst.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory training an analyst who will work toward the Water Quality Analyst certificate under Regulation 128/04.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the analyst first day through supervised routine work.

cards.label: Complete laboratory safety orientation and read the safety procedures
Read the standard operating procedures for the assigned methods
Observe a trained analyst performing each assigned method
Perform the method under direct supervision with results checked
Complete the initial demonstration of capability for each method
Begin routine work with results reviewed until competency is signed off

tasks.explanation: Competency is built in order: safety and procedures first, then observation, supervised practice, a formal capability demonstration, and reviewed routine work.

tasks.prompt: Order the initial demonstration of capability steps for a bench method.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional analyst qualifying on a chemistry method for the first time.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing the capability samples through the qualification decision.

cards.label: Prepare or obtain the capability samples of known concentration for the method
Have the analyst analyze the samples without assistance on a normal batch
Calculate the analyst results and compare them with the known values
Confirm accuracy and precision meet the method qualification criteria
Record the demonstration with samples, results, and reviewer signature
Authorize the analyst for independent work on that method or assign more training

tasks.explanation: The demonstration uses known samples analyzed unaided, judged against set criteria, and ends in a signed authorization or a clear decision for more training.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual competency review steps for a certified analyst.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory completing the yearly review for its analysts.
tasks.configuration: Scope: gathering the analyst records through the signed review.

cards.label: Gather the analyst proficiency results, quality records, and training file
Review the analyst results on control charts and duplicate performance
Check that required refresher training and procedure updates were completed
Discuss performance and any development goals with the analyst
Record the review outcome and any assigned training with dates
File the signed review in the analyst training record

tasks.explanation: The annual review is evidence based, drawing on proficiency and quality performance, and it produces dated training actions rather than a general impression.

tasks.prompt: Order the training steps when a revised procedure is issued.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional laboratory issuing a revised titration procedure.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the revision being approved through analysts working to the new version.

cards.label: Issue the revised procedure with the changes summarized for staff
Brief all analysts who use the procedure on the changes
Have each analyst read the revision and sign the training acknowledgement
Observe the first use of the revised steps where the change affects technique
Withdraw and archive the superseded procedure copies
Record the completed training in each analyst training file

tasks.explanation: A revision only takes effect when affected analysts are briefed, acknowledge the new version, and old copies are withdrawn so no one works from superseded steps.

tasks.prompt: A method blank in a metals batch reads 0.08 mg/L for lead while all drinking water samples in the batch read below 0.01 mg/L.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The method blank was prepared with reagent water and a new bottle from lot B-214 and carried through the full digestion.
A second blank prepared in an older bottle from lot B-198 reads below detection for lead.
A blank prepared with reagent water in a lot B-214 bottle but without digestion also reads 0.07 mg/L for lead.
The calibration check standard recovers at 99 percent and the instrument blank of plain acid reads below detection.
Samples collected in lot B-198 bottles all read below 0.01 mg/L for lead.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Lead is leaching from the new bottle lot B-214 into blanks and would bias results high
The samples truly contain no lead and the blank result is an instrument drift artifact
The digestion acid is contaminated with lead
The calibration standard was prepared too low, inflating the blank

inference.explanation: Only lot B-214 blanks are elevated, including one that skipped digestion, while lot B-198 blanks, the plain acid blank, and the check standard are clean. That isolates the bottle lot, not the acid, instrument, or calibration.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the bottle lot as the source?

options.label: Quarantine and lot acceptance records for bottle lot B-214, including a leach test on unused bottles
Instrument maintenance log for the metals analyser
Field sampling schedule for the week

nextClue.explanation: A leach test on unused lot B-214 bottles directly tests whether the bottles themselves release lead.

clueText.nc-a: Unused lot B-214 bottles leached 0.06 to 0.09 mg/L lead into reagent water, while lot B-198 bottles leached none, confirming the lot.
clueText.nc-b: The analyser log shows routine service only, with no fault that would affect one bottle lot.
clueText.nc-c: The schedule shows normal sampling times and says nothing about bottle materials.

tasks.prompt: Every field blank in a weekly microbiology run grows total coliform, while the matching distribution samples are all absent.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: Field blanks were sterile water poured into sample bottles at each site and handled like samples.
The laboratory method blank of sterile water opened only in the lab is absent for total coliform.
All field blanks used bottles from sterile lot S-88; distribution samples used lot S-87 bottles.
A field blank repeated in a lot S-87 bottle at the same site is absent for total coliform.
Incubator temperature records and media sterility checks are within limits.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The lot S-88 sample bottles were not sterile and contaminated the field blanks
The distribution system water is contaminated at every site
The incubator temperature caused false growth in all bottles
The analyst contaminated every bottle during plating

inference.explanation: Field blanks fail only in lot S-88 bottles, the lab blank is clean, and a repeat blank in a lot S-87 bottle is clean. Distribution samples in lot S-87 are absent, so system contamination, incubator fault, and analyst handling do not fit.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the bottle sterility failure?

options.label: Supplier sterility certificate and lab sterility check results for lot S-88
Distribution pressure records for the sampling day
Incubator calibration certificate

nextClue.explanation: The sterility check on lot S-88 directly tests whether that lot was sterile on receipt.

clueText.nc-a: The lab sterility check found growth in 3 of 10 unopened lot S-88 bottles, and the supplier certificate was for a different lot, confirming the failure.
clueText.nc-b: Pressures were normal all day, which does not explain growth only in one bottle lot.
clueText.nc-c: The incubator certificate is current, matching the in-limit temperature records.

tasks.prompt: A reagent blank for nitrate reads 1.4 mg/L as N in one batch, and low level samples in the same batch all read about 1 mg/L higher than their duplicates run the next day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The suspect batch used a freshly opened bottle of colour reagent from lot R-41.
The next day duplicates used colour reagent from lot R-40 and a fresh reagent blank that read below 0.1 mg/L.
A reagent blank made with lot R-41 reagent in a clean tube still reads 1.3 mg/L as N.
The spectrophotometer zero and calibration check with lot R-40 reagent are within limits.
No samples in either batch were preserved or stored differently.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Colour reagent lot R-41 is contaminated with nitrate and biased the first batch high
The samples degraded overnight and lost nitrate before the duplicate run
The spectrophotometer drifted high for one day only
The first analyst misread the sample volumes

inference.explanation: The high blank follows lot R-41 even in a clean tube, while lot R-40 blanks and checks are clean and duplicates drop by the blank amount. Degradation would not raise a reagent blank, and drift is cleared by the passing checks.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the reagent lot problem?

options.label: Reagent lot acceptance log and blank results by reagent lot for the past month
Sample refrigerator temperature log
Analyst training file

nextClue.explanation: Blank results grouped by reagent lot show whether high blanks track lot R-41 only.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows every lot R-41 blank above 1.2 mg/L and every lot R-40 blank below 0.1 mg/L over the month, confirming the lot.
clueText.nc-b: Refrigerator temperatures were in range, which does not explain a reagent blank prepared fresh.
clueText.nc-c: The training file shows current certification, which does not track reagent lots.

tasks.prompt: A trip blank for volatile organics detects chloroform at 12 ug/L, while all well samples in the cooler are below detection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The trip blank travelled unopened in the same cooler as the well samples.
A laboratory storage blank kept in the lab refrigerator reads below detection for chloroform.
The cooler also carried a leaking bottle of chloroform containing laboratory solvent in a separate unsealed bag.
A second trip blank in a different cooler without the solvent bag reads below detection.
All vials were sealed with no headspace and holding times were met.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Chloroform vapour from the leaking solvent bottle contaminated the trip blank in transit
The wells are contaminated with chloroform that the samples failed to show
The laboratory refrigerator contaminated all blanks
The vials lost chloroform from the samples by volatilization

inference.explanation: Only the blank sharing a cooler with the leaking solvent is positive, while the lab blank and the blank in the clean cooler are negative and the well samples are negative. That points to transit vapour exposure, not the wells or the lab.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the transit contamination route?

options.label: Cooler packing and chain of custody notes plus the solvent bottle inspection record
Well pumping records for the sampling day
Laboratory refrigerator temperature log

nextClue.explanation: Packing notes and the bottle inspection show whether solvent and blanks shared an unsealed cooler space.

clueText.nc-a: Notes confirm the solvent bottle cap was cracked and packed unsealed in the same cooler, and the bottle lost volume in transit.
clueText.nc-b: Pumping records were normal and cannot explain a positive unopened blank.
clueText.nc-c: Refrigerator temperatures were in range and the storage blank was clean.

tasks.prompt: Method blanks for fluoride read 0.4 mg/L on Monday only, and Monday samples near the 1.5 mg/L standard all need review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: Monday blanks used deionized water from carboy C-2; Tuesday blanks from carboy C-1 read below 0.05 mg/L.
A blank of bottled certified reagent water analysed Monday reads below 0.05 mg/L.
Carboy C-2 was refilled Friday from a resin system whose service light was on.
The fluoride electrode calibration slope and check standard were within limits on both days.
Monday and Tuesday samples were analysed on the same electrode with the same buffers.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The deionized water in carboy C-2 was contaminated with fluoride and raised Monday blanks
The electrode drifted on Monday and recovered on Tuesday
The buffers were contaminated on Monday only
Monday samples truly rose by 0.4 mg/L across the system

inference.explanation: Monday blanks are high only when made with carboy C-2 water, certified water blanks are clean, and electrode checks pass both days. The shared buffers and electrode clear drift and buffer causes, leaving the carboy water.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the carboy contamination?

options.label: Deionized water system service log and resistivity records for carboy C-2
Electrode purchase invoice
Sample login schedule

nextClue.explanation: Service and resistivity records show whether the resin system feeding carboy C-2 had failed.

clueText.nc-a: Resistivity for C-2 fell well below specification after the Friday refill and the resin was past its service date, confirming poor water quality.
clueText.nc-b: The invoice only dates the electrode purchase and says nothing about water quality.
clueText.nc-c: The login schedule shows normal receipt times on both days.

tasks.prompt: Total coliform is detected in a laboratory blank that was opened beside a strongly positive raw water sample during setup.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The blank was sterile water in a sealed bottle opened on the same bench at the same time as the raw water sample.
A second blank opened later in a separate clean area is absent for total coliform.
The raw water sample beside the blank reads too numerous to count for total coliform.
Media sterility plates from the same lot show no growth.
A blank carried through the full method without being opened beside the raw sample is absent.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Aerosol or splash carryover from the high count raw sample contaminated the open blank during setup
The sterile water supply itself is contaminated
The media lot is contaminated
The incubator is contaminated and grows coliform on all plates

inference.explanation: Only the blank opened beside the very high count raw sample is positive, while sealed method blanks, the clean area blank, and media sterility plates are clean. That fits local carryover during setup, not the water, media, or incubator.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the setup carryover?

options.label: Bench setup log and repeat blank results after separating raw and blank handling
Media supplier invoice
Incubator door seal inspection

nextClue.explanation: Repeat blanks run after separating raw and blank handling test whether the practice change removes the positives.

clueText.nc-a: After raw and blank handling were separated, 20 consecutive blanks were absent, confirming setup carryover as the cause.
clueText.nc-b: The invoice confirms media delivery only and does not address bench practice.
clueText.nc-c: The door seal was intact, matching the clean sterility plates.

tasks.prompt: A new lot of sample bottles gives low chlorine residuals in every sample preserved for bench chlorine checks compared with field readings.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: Field free chlorine at collection averages 0.80 mg/L; lab results on the new bottles average 0.30 mg/L for split samples.
Splits collected in the previous bottle lot match field readings within 0.05 mg/L.
The new bottles were not rinsed with sample and carry a visible white residue.
A chlorine demand test shows the residue consumes 0.5 mg/L chlorine in reagent water.
Holding time and temperature for both lots were the same and within limits.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Residue in the new bottle lot exerts chlorine demand and lowers residuals before analysis
The field chlorine meter reads high
Chlorine decayed naturally during a longer holding time for the new lot
The laboratory DPD reagent has expired

inference.explanation: Splits in the old lot match the field meter, holding times are equal, and the residue alone consumes 0.5 mg/L in reagent water. That isolates bottle residue demand, not the meter, decay time, or reagent.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the bottle residue problem?

options.label: Bottle lot washing and acceptance test results for the new lot
Field meter calibration log
DPD reagent expiry list

nextClue.explanation: Acceptance testing of the new lot measures chlorine demand of unused bottles directly.

clueText.nc-a: Unused new lot bottles consumed 0.45 to 0.55 mg/L chlorine in demand free water, while the old lot consumed under 0.05 mg/L.
clueText.nc-b: The field meter log shows passing checks, matching the old lot split agreement.
clueText.nc-c: The DPD reagent is in date, and old lot splits using it matched the field.

tasks.prompt: Blanks for total phosphorus read high only in batches digested in the older block digester, not in the new digester.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: Both digesters use the same reagents, tubes from one lot, and the same analyst on the same day.
Blanks digested in the old block read 0.06 mg/L; blanks in the new block read below 0.01 mg/L.
The old block wells show heavy scale and residue when inspected with a light.
A blank digested in the old block in a brand new tube still reads 0.05 mg/L.
Calibration and check standards that are not digested read correctly.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Residue in the old digester wells contaminates tubes during digestion
The reagent lot is contaminated with phosphorus
The tube lot is contaminated
The colorimeter calibration has drifted

inference.explanation: The same reagents and tubes give clean blanks in the new block and high blanks in the old block, and new tubes still pick up phosphorus in the old block. Shared reagents and tubes and passing undigested checks clear the other options.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms digester well contamination?

options.label: Digester cleaning log and blank results before and after a deep clean of the old block
Reagent delivery record
Colorimeter lamp replacement record

nextClue.explanation: Blanks before and after cleaning the old block test whether removing well residue removes the contamination.

clueText.nc-a: After a deep clean, old block blanks fell below 0.01 mg/L for five batches, confirming well residue as the source.
clueText.nc-b: The delivery record shows one reagent lot used in both blocks, so it cannot explain the difference.
clueText.nc-c: The lamp record is routine and checks passed without digestion.

tasks.prompt: E. coli is reported in a method blank, and the same batch has one distribution sample positive that cannot be confirmed on resampling.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The blank and the positive sample were filtered on the same manifold positions in sequence.
The manifold was disinfected between samples on other runs but the disinfection step was skipped in this run, per the bench sheet.
A blank filtered first in a later run with disinfection between positions is absent.
Source water and other distribution samples in the batch are absent for E. coli.
Media lot sterility and incubator checks pass.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Cross contamination on the shared manifold from a prior positive sample caused the blank and sample positives
The distribution system had a genuine E. coli event at one site only
The media lot grows E. coli without any sample
The incubator temperature created false E. coli colonies

inference.explanation: The skipped disinfection step, positives following sequence on one manifold, and clean blanks when disinfection is done point to manifold carryover. Media and incubator checks pass, and a genuine single site event would not explain the blank.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms manifold carryover?

options.label: Manifold disinfection log and ordered filtration sequence for the batch
Distribution main break records
Media lot sterility certificate

nextClue.explanation: The sequence and disinfection log show whether positives followed a positive sample without disinfection.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows the blank and sample were filtered immediately after a known positive with no disinfection recorded, confirming the carryover path.
clueText.nc-b: No main breaks were recorded that week, and a break would not contaminate a lab blank.
clueText.nc-c: The sterility certificate is clean, matching the passing media checks.

tasks.prompt: A batch blank for turbidity reads 0.45 NTU while treated water samples read 0.06 to 0.10 NTU, reversing the usual pattern.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The blank was reagent water poured into a sample cell that had been used for a raw water sample and only rinsed once.
The same reagent water in a dedicated clean cell reads 0.03 NTU.
The turbidimeter zero with a sealed standard cell is within limits.
Raw water that day read 18 NTU and left visible film on cells.
A second blank in the clean cell after the batch also reads 0.04 NTU.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The sample cell carried over raw water film and raised the blank reading
The reagent water supply became turbid
The turbidimeter lamp drifted during the batch
The treated water samples were diluted before reading

inference.explanation: The same reagent water reads low in a clean cell and high in the once rinsed raw water cell, and the instrument zero passes. That is cell carryover, not the water supply, lamp, or sample dilution.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms cell carryover?

options.label: Cell cleaning log and blank readings by cell identifier for the batch
Reagent water system log
Lamp hour meter reading

nextClue.explanation: Blank readings grouped by cell show whether high blanks follow one cell only.

clueText.nc-a: All blanks above 0.3 NTU used cell 4, the raw water cell, and all clean cell blanks were below 0.05 NTU, confirming carryover.
clueText.nc-b: The water system log shows normal resistivity, matching the clean cell results.
clueText.nc-c: Lamp hours are within life and the zero check passed.

tasks.prompt: A laboratory audit finds calibration records for a turbidimeter signed as complete for a week when the instrument was out of service awaiting a lamp.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The maintenance log shows the turbidimeter tagged out all week with no lamp installed.
Calibration signatures for that week exist in the record book with passing values.
No turbidity results were reported from that instrument that week; a backup meter was used and its records are genuine.
The backup meter calibration records are separate and verifiable.
The signer was on duty that week, per the roster.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Calibration records were signed for work that could not have been performed on the out of service instrument
The maintenance log dates are wrong and the instrument was in service
The backup meter records were mistaken for the main meter records
Passing values prove the calibrations truly occurred

inference.explanation: The instrument was physically incapable of calibration without a lamp, maintenance tagging is documented, and genuine backup records exist separately. Signed passing values cannot prove work on a tagged out instrument, and the records are not the backup's, which are separate.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the false records?

options.label: Maintenance tag out log and calibration record book for the turbidimeter
Backup meter calibration file alone
Lamp delivery invoice alone

nextClue.explanation: Tag out status against signed calibrations is the direct contradiction.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows a continuous tag out with lamp removal, while the book shows daily passing calibrations, confirming records for work not performed.
clueText.nc-b: Backup records are genuine and separate, so they do not explain the main meter book.
clueText.nc-c: The invoice dates the lamp arrival after the signed week, supporting the tag out.

tasks.prompt: Preserved metals blanks from one sampler show copper at 0.20 mg/L while blanks from three other samplers are below detection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: All blanks used the same acid lot, bottle lot, and reagent water.
The one sampler used a brass fitting on the sampling tap manifold; the others used stainless fittings.
A blank drawn through a stainless fitting at the same site reads below detection for copper.
Laboratory blanks that never left the lab read below detection.
The instrument calibration and check standards pass.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The brass fitting leached copper into that sampler's blanks during collection
The acid preservative is contaminated with copper
The laboratory instrument has a copper memory effect
All sites sampled by that sampler have high copper in the water

inference.explanation: Only the brass fitting sampler is affected, shared acid, bottles, and water are clean in lab blanks, and a stainless fitting blank at the same site is clean. That isolates the brass fitting, not the acid, instrument, or sites.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the fitting as the source?

options.label: Sampling equipment log identifying fitting materials by sampler, with paired blank results
Acid supplier certificate
Instrument tune report

nextClue.explanation: Paired blanks by fitting material directly compare brass and stainless collection paths.

clueText.nc-a: Paired results show brass path blanks at 0.18 to 0.22 mg/L copper and stainless path blanks below detection at the same sites.
clueText.nc-b: The acid certificate is for the shared lot that gave clean lab blanks.
clueText.nc-c: The tune report passed, matching the passing check standards.

tasks.prompt: A sterility blank for a new autoclave load of bottles fails, and all samples in those bottles are held for review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drinking water laboratory case under Regulation 169/03 and Regulation 170/03. All results are from the stated batch unless noted, and archived laboratory records are available for review.

evidence.label: The autoclave printout for the load shows the temperature reached only 110 C for 5 minutes instead of 121 C for 15 minutes.
Bottles from the previous autoclave load pass their sterility blank.
The chemical indicator tape on the failed load did not change to the full sterilized colour.
Media and incubator checks for the batch pass.
No samples had been opened before the sterility result was known.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The autoclave cycle failed to sterilize the bottle load
The sterility blank water was contaminated before autoclaving
The incubator contaminated the sterility blank
The indicator tape lot is defective

inference.explanation: The printout shows a short, low temperature cycle, the tape agrees it did not sterilize, and the previous load passed. Incubator and media checks pass, so the failure is the autoclave cycle itself.
